application_guidance.input_pattern: A fixed lower gradient direction and a linear lower perturbation with Lipschitz lower Hessian blocks.
read_original_when: Changing the perturbation to t f(x,y), refreshing the direction during the solve, or changing the upper evaluation point
sensitive_conditions: Keep a frozen throughout the tilted solve
Use the unperturbed y0 in f_x
ρ=0 exactness concerns the ideal component only

content.intended_use: Control the ideal frozen-direction component; it is not an oracle complexity theorem.

proofs.full_local_argument: For fixed x, adding a linear function preserves μ-strong convexity and coercivity, so each y_t(a) exists uniquely and satisfies g_y(x,y_t(a))=−ta. Since g_y(x,y0)=0, strong monotonicity gives μ||y_t(a)−y0||²≤t|<a,y_t(a)−y0>|≤tC_f||y_t(a)−y0||. Division when nonzero proves the displacement inequality, and the zero case is immediate. Applying the same argument to two tilted stationarity equations gives ||y_t(a)−y_t(a′)||≤(t/μ)||a−a′||. Because g_x is L_g-Lipschitz in y, subtracting h_t(a) and h_t(a′) proves its k-Lipschitz bound. For bias put d=y_t(a0)−y0, H=g_yy(x,y0), B=g_xy(x,y0). H is symmetric with H⪰μI, ||H^−1||≤1/μ and ||B||≤L_g. The implicit function theorem applied to g_y(x,y*(x))=0 gives ∇F(x)=f_x(x,y0)−BH^−1a0. The Taylor-integral errors e_y=∫_0^1[g_yy(x,y0+sd)−H]d ds and e_x=∫_0^1[g_xy(x,y0+sd)−B]d ds satisfy ||e_y||,||e_x||≤ρ||d||²/2. Stationarity gives Hd+e_y=−ta0, hence d/t=−H^−1a0−H^−1e_y/t. Substitution into h_t yields h_t(a0)−∇F(x)=−BH^−1e_y/t+e_x/t. Its norm is at most (1+L_g/μ)ρ||d||²/(2t), and ||d||≤tC_f/μ gives Eρt. When ρ=0 both integral errors vanish, proving exactness. If Eρ>0 the stated minimum for t has Eρt≤ε/128; if Eρ=0 the bias is zero for t=1. None of these steps removes stochastic batch error or approximate-inner-solve error.
proofs.locator: Appendix B.1, p.17; complete local reconstruction
map: Strong monotonicity gives displacement and direction sensitivity.
Taylor-integral remainders plus the implicit hypergradient identity give the bias coefficient.
proofs.omitted_details: None for these local inequalities; no implementation or outer convergence is proved here.
proofs.reading_coverage: Original PDF p.17 directly extracted and initial p.17 image personally inspected; assumptions checked on pp.5–6.

assumptions: Over full Euclidean lower space g(x,·) is μ-strongly convex, μ>0; the required continuous Hessian blocks exist, Lip(∇g)≤L_g globally, and g_yy,g_xy are jointly ρ-Lipschitz.
f is continuously differentiable with ||f_y||≤C_f; the source standing smoothness assumptions ensure differentiability of F=f(x,y*(x)).
Directions a,a′ lie in the Euclidean ball ||a||,||a′||≤C_f; t>0. Exact lower solutions and exact gradients here define an ideal mathematical quantity, not available free SFO responses.
statement.conclusion: ||y_t(a)−y0||≤tC_f/μ; ||y_t(a)−y_t(a′)||≤(t/μ)||a−a′||; ||h_t(a)−h_t(a′)||≤k||a−a′||; ||h_t(a0)−∇F(x)||≤Eρt. At ρ=0 the ideal h_t(a0) equals ∇F(x) for every t>0. For ε>0 choose t=1 if Eρ=0 and otherwise t=min{1,ε/(128Eρ)}, giving bias ≤ε/128.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For fixed x∈R^{d_x}, y0=y*(x), a0=f_y(x,y0), y_t(a)=argmin_y[g(x,y)+t<a,y>], h_t(a)=f_x(x,y0)+[g_x(x,y_t(a))−g_x(x,y0)]/t. Let k=L_g/μ and Eρ=(1+k)ρC_f²/(2μ²).
statement.parameter_domains: Finite dimensions; μ>0, L_g≥μ, C_f≥0, ρ≥0, t>0. Neither Δ nor R0 nor positive noise is needed for these local inequalities.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such x,t,a,a′ the following deterministic inequalities hold; there is no stochastic success event or algorithm-class quantifier.

use_restrictions: Complete local argument is supplied for independent checking; no Reviewer acceptance is claimed.
Does not imply zero implementation error at ρ=0 or grant free exact inner solutions.

facets.subject: Deterministic inequalities for every fixed x,t and admissible direction
Ideal vector h_t(a), not an outer stationary point

research_use.reason: Freezing a0 leaves approximation bias governed by lower Hessian variation.

summary: At fixed x, frozen linear tilt gives displacement tC_f/μ, direction Lipschitz constants t/μ and L_g/μ, and hypergradient bias at most (1+L_g/μ)ρC_f²t/(2μ²).
title: Frozen-linear-tilt deterministic bias and direction stability
use_when: Separate ideal deterministic approximation bias from stochastic implementation error.
